verses.1: He also went to Derbium and Lystra. There, he met a disciple named Timotheus, who was the son of a Jewish woman who was very pious. His father was Greek.
verses.2: Who was accused by those in Lysistra and Ikonios’s brothers.
verses.3: At that moment, Paul decided to leave with him. He took him along, and passed him along to the Jews who lived in those places. After all, everyone knew that his father was a Greek.
verses.4: And when they traveled from city to city, they were given the authority to enforce the teachings that had been taught by the apostles and elders in Jerusalem.
verses.5: And so, the churches became more numerous day by day, as their number increased.
verses.6: We then went into the regions of Phrygia and Galatia. There, under the influence of the Holy Spirit, we preached the word in Asia.
verses.7: And when they came along the Myssian road, they tried to go into Bithynia. But the Spirit of Jesus did not allow them to do so.
verses.8: After that, they went down to Troas.
verses.9: And at that time, through the night, Paul arrived. There was a man from Macedonia who came to him and asked him, “Please help us when you go to Macedonia.”
verses.10: And when we saw this sign, we immediately decided to go to Makedonia. We believed that God had called us to preach to them.
verses.11: Thus, having left Troyad, we continued our journey towards Samothrace. From there, we went on to the city of Neapoli.
verses.12: From there, we went to Philippi, which is the first city in Macedonia. It was a colony. We spent several days in this city.
verses.13: On that day of the Sabbaths, we went outside the gate, along a river that we consider to be a place of prayer. There, we sat down and talked with the women who were also there.
verses.14: And there was a woman named Lydia, who lived in the city of Thυατείρων. She respected the god greatly. She heard that the Lord had commanded her to pay attention to those who spoke under the influence of Paul’s teachings.
verses.15: And when she and her family were baptized, she called out to them, saying, “If you truly believe me to be a trustworthy person, then come into my house.” And we were healed.
verses.16: As we were being led towards the prayer, a little girl with healing powers came to our aid. She performed many miracles for her master, who was very grateful to her.
verses.17: This teaching, which Paul and we also follow, says: These are people who are slaves to the god of kings; they will lead you on a path of salvation.
verses.18: He did this for many days. When Pilate became angry, he returned to the spirit and said, “I command you to leave her immediately.” And so, in that hour, he left her.
verses.19: Seeing that their leaders realized that their hopes for achieving their goals had been disappointed, they brought Paul and Silas to the marketplace where the rulers were.
verses.20: And when they brought them before the generals, they said, “These people will destroy our city, as the Jews currently rule over it.”
verses.21: And they will also admit that it is not right for us to accept or do anything that would be unacceptable to the Romans.
verses.22: And the crowd also became enraged by them. The commanders ordered that their heads be cut off.
verses.23: Many people who came to them caused them harm and put them in prison. They ordered the guards to keep them safely in custody.
verses.24: He, upon receiving such a request, put them into the inner prison, and also secured their feet with ropes.
verses.25: But according to the Middle East tradition, Paul and Silas prayed to the God. Meanwhile, those who were bound by ropes were also affected by this prayer.
verses.26: A great earthquake occurred, so that the foundations of the bridge were destroyed. All the gates were broken open, and all the bonds were broken apart.
verses.27: The prison guard, who became insane, saw that the doors of the prison were broken open. He tried to kill himself by cutting his own throat, thinking that in doing so he would be able to escape from his bonds.
verses.28: Then Paul said in a loud voice, “Do not do anything that would harm yourself. After all, we are all together here.”
verses.29: When he asked for light, he rushed in. Then, becoming exhausted, he approached Paul and Silas.
verses.30: And when he brought them outside, he said, “My lords, what should I do in order to be saved?”
verses.31: And they said, “Trust in the Lord Jesus. Then you and your household will be saved.”
verses.32: And they spoke to him the words of the Lord, along with all those who were in his house.
verses.33: And when he took them away that night, he treated them for their injuries. He baptized himself and all those who were with him as well.
verses.34: After bringing them into the house, a table was placed there, and he was filled with joy, as if he had seen God.
verses.35: On the day that it happened, the generals sent out the rabdomachers, saying, “Kill those people.”
verses.36: The prison guard reported these words to Paul, saying that the generals had sent for him so that he could be released. Now, therefore, go away in peace.
verses.37: And Paul said to them, “They have put us in prison because they saw that we were not conforming to their rules. And now they want to release us from prison? No, they actually brought us here themselves.”
verses.38: The soldiers were told by the rabdusians these words. They were afraid when they heard that it was Romans who said those words.
verses.39: And when they came, they called out to them. Then, with the help of their followers, they were driven away from the city.
verses.40: After leaving the prison, they went towards Lydius’s place. When they arrived there, they called upon their brothers, and then they set out on their journey.
